clue.text: Licence to mix with epic

definitions.note: the answer is the word that goes before licence in the phrase poetic licence

indicators.note: to mix things is to stir them together into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Permission to blend into a grand heroic tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works as a fill-in: the answer is the first half of the phrase whose second half the clue gives.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic licence is the freedom writers of verse take to bend grammar or fact, so the answer completes that phrase.

clue.text: It isn't acuteness that discovers iron between church and town

parts.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church

indicators.note: read as dis-covers, it takes the covering letter off the front and puts it elsewhere, so the word is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: A riddle about something that finds metal lying between a church and a town.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged iron sits between church and town, giving CH-RONI-CITY.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine an illness is either acute (sudden, short) or chronic (lasting), so chronicity is the condition opposite to acuteness.

clue.text: Case of Paul holding Matthews (11 10)

indicators.note: one thing holding another has it inside it

parts.note: Paul Ince, England footballer of the 1990s
Sir Stanley Matthews, England footballer; 11 10 is association football

explanation.surface: An example of one footballer marking another.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference 11 10 points to ASSOCIATION FOOTBALL, telling you both names are footballers: Paul Ince holds Stan Matthews, IN-STAN-CE.
explanation.definitionFit: A case and an instance are both a single example or occurrence of something, as in 'in this case'.

clue.text: George Gordon frequently intervened between male and female (Roth's work)

parts.note: a cock is a male bird

indicators.note: a piece of work is something made, so the name is worked into a new order

parts.note: oft is an old word for often
a hen is a female bird
the novelist Philip Roth, taken as written then rearranged

explanation.surface: Lord Byron (George Gordon) often came between a man and a woman, as in a Philip Roth novel.
explanation.walkthrough: George Gordon looks like Byron, but it is the 5th Duke of Gordon, whose nickname this is. Oft is an old word for often.
explanation.definitionFit: Cock o' the North was the nickname of George Gordon, 5th Duke of Gordon, a Scottish nobleman and soldier.

clue.text: Contest in the round with increased number in the bag

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: a bag or haul of fish or game is a catch
prices that have increased are up
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a number

explanation.surface: A boxing contest with a growing sum of money riding on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the bag' sounds like a certain win, but the bag is a haul, and 'in' is doing the placing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup match is a knockout fixture played in one round of a cup competition, such as the FA Cup.

clue.text: Sold out in centre of viral infection

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: the core is the centre of something

indicators.note: out here means disordered, put out of place

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Tickets sold out at the heart of an outbreak.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold sore is a blister round the lips caused by the herpes simplex virus, so it is an infection by a virus.

clue.text: See 4
Unhappy motoring is a bore, interrupting the caviar?

indicators.note: something interrupting breaks into the middle of another thing

parts.note: caviar is the salted roe of the sturgeon
taken as written
a drag is a tedious thing, a bore

explanation.surface: Complaining that driving is tedious, and comparing it to a disrupted luxury snack.
explanation.walkthrough: A DRAG breaks into ROE: RO-ADRAG-E. The question mark flags that caviar is only one kind of roe.
explanation.definitionFit: Road rage is the violent anger some drivers show towards others, a decidedly unhappy experience behind the wheel.

clue.text: See 21
Front page held up for Roman governor?

parts.note: the front page is page one, P1, with the 1 read as the letter I
a train held up runs late

explanation.surface: A newspaper's lead story was delayed, waiting on news of a Roman official.
explanation.walkthrough: P1 is page one, and the digit 1 doubles as the letter I in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontius Pilate was the Roman prefect of Judea who presided at the trial of Jesus; the question mark marks him as one example.

clue.text: Authority in 11 10 performing a solo on FBI coat-tails

indicators.note: letters performing are acting out a new routine, so they take a new order

parts.note: every letter of these words, taken as written

explanation.surface: An agent in tails giving a solo turn in the game's governing body.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 10 read in that order is ASSOCIATION FOOTBALL, the game this body governs; the answer is the same two words the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Football Association is the governing body of soccer in England, the sport formally called association football.

clue.text: See 10
The complete bird gets to move quite briskly

definitions.note: noun phrase: a movement taken quite briskly

parts.note: the complete amount is all of it
an egret is a white heron
taken as written

explanation.surface: A whole flock of birds is made to get going fairly quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: Move reads as a verb, but here it is a noun, short for movement in a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegretto is a musical tempo marking, a little slower than allegro, and names a movement played at that lively pace.

clue.text: Conservatives dug a lord out

indicators.note: out here means disordered, put out of its usual arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Traditionalists dug up an aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: The old guard are the long-standing members of a group who resist change, a body of traditionalists.

clue.text: Black and white listen to Spooner's green space

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of the two words are swapped, after the slip-prone Oxford don

parts.note: pied means black and white, like a magpie; hark means listen

explanation.surface: An instruction to hear a magpie-coloured patch of grass.
explanation.walkthrough: The swapped sounds give HIED PARK, said like HYDE PARK, the large royal park in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyde Park is a large public park in central London, an open green space in the city.

clue.text: Beast eating artist for dessert?

indicators.note: something eating another takes it inside itself

parts.note: a camel is a beast of burden
RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's usual artist

explanation.surface: A wild animal devours a painter for pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that caramel is more a toffee flavour than a dessert in itself, as in crème caramel.
explanation.definitionFit: Caramel is cooked sugar used in sweets and puddings such as crème caramel, so it stands for a sweet course.

clue.text: Girl left on Cumbrian coast

definitions.note: a phrase of place standing for the town: fair because the answer is a place found on that coast

parts.note: a girl's name
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A young woman abandoned on the seashore of north-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: Cumbria is the county in the far north-west of England, home of the Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Maryport is a small harbour town on the coast of Cumbria, facing the Solway Firth.

clue.text: Perfectly prepared to die for one's friend

indicators.note: something prepared has been made ready, worked into a new form

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
an ally is a friend on one's side

explanation.surface: Someone ready to lay down their life for a friend, which is a perfect sacrifice.
explanation.walkthrough: Prepared looks like part of the surface's 'prepared to die', but it reworks the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideally means in the best or most perfect way, as in an ideally placed house.

clue.text: Game gets warmer through the French fever

parts.note: a rug is a blanket that keeps you warm
by means through, as in 'by way of'
le is the French for the
an ague is a malarial fever

explanation.surface: A game gets heated up by a French fever.
explanation.walkthrough: Warmer looks like a comparative adjective but is a noun: something that warms.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby league is the thirteen-a-side version of rugby football, a sport or game.

clue.text: Involve keeping things in the family

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to have as a necessary consequence
second meaning: a legal settlement passing property down a fixed line of heirs

explanation.surface: Getting involved means keeping secrets within the family.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail is to require something as a consequence; an entail is a legal restriction keeping an estate within one line of descendants.

clue.text: See 7
Release? Don't release — they can't take it from you
Expose drug made by jet?

parts.note: to air something is to expose it
speed is slang for amphetamine

explanation.surface: Revealing a narcotic produced by a dark black gemstone.
explanation.walkthrough: Made reads as a verb in the surface; in the definition it means achieved, the speed a jet makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Airspeed is an aircraft's speed relative to the air around it, which a jet makes as it flies.

clue.text: Too much Scotch, not at home capital

parts.note: OTT is short for over the top
awa is the Scots spelling of away

explanation.surface: Too much whisky, so not at home in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotch looks like whisky, but it marks the Scots form of away, meaning not at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the capital city of Canada, in the province of Ontario.

clue.text: Say nasty things about river container

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
a crate is a box for goods

explanation.surface: Insulting a vessel on a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to curse or denounce someone vehemently, speaking of them with loathing.

clue.text: Little creature in Richard II's speech?

indicators.note: speech points to how the name is pronounced, not how it is spelt

parts.note: Dick is short for Richard, and II means two of him

explanation.surface: A small animal featuring in one of the King's monologues in Shakespeare's history play.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard II looks like Shakespeare's king; read it as two Richards, Dick and Dick.
explanation.definitionFit: A dik-dik is a tiny African antelope, barely a foot tall at the shoulder.
